name: Play READ_CONTACTS declaration
plain: Google adds a Contacts permission declaration so apps use the Contact Picker when possible.
meaning: Contact lists are valuable for growth hacks and ads. Policy effective 28 October 2026 asks apps to justify broad access, mirroring photo and video rules.

android.store_policy: Declaration effective 28 Oct 2026 (per Play policy announcement); Contact Picker preferred
android.note: Dates should be confirmed in Play Console before relying on them.

ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.1; iOS 18 limited contacts access

limits.headline: Can only access all your contacts on Android if Google approves the reason
limits.user_action: You tap Pick contacts, or Allow contacts when the app asks
can: Show a contact picker where you choose one or a few people
Use all contacts if Google approved a core need
Share a limited set of contacts (iOS 18)
cannot: Take your full contact list for growth or ads without approval
Skip the justification form that starts on 28 October 2026 (confirm dates in Play Console)
See contacts you did not share when you chose limited access (iOS 18)
limits.reach_label: Contacts you pick, or all if approved
limits.differs: iOS 18 lets you share only some contacts. Android moves to a picker unless Google approves wider access.

story.what_it_is: Google's new rule that apps explain why they want your whole contact list.

marketing.name: READ_CONTACTS permission declaration
marketing.pitch: Apps are asked to use the Contact Picker when possible, and explain broad contact access.

story.for_you: Instead of handing over your whole address book, you may now pick just the contacts you want to share. You keep the rest private.
story.for_makers: Contact lists fuel growth hacks, such as friend finders and invite spam, and ad matching. The policy, effective 28 October 2026, pushes makers toward a picker unless they truly need the full list.

use_cases.example: A new social app asks to find friends and now uses a picker so you choose who is invited.
A messenger needs the full list to show which contacts already use it, and must justify that.
A payment app picks one contact to send money to instead of reading all numbers.
A game offers a 'invite friends' button that opens a picker and sends one text at a time.
An ad broker used contact lists to build a social graph, which this rule makes harder.
A caller ID app needs contacts to label callers and must show it as a core feature.

story.android_note: Google's Contact Picker lets the person share only chosen contacts.
story.ios_note: iOS 18 added limited contacts access, with a similar choice.

technical_bounds: Android date to be confirmed in console

abuse: Uploading address books for growth or ads
